literal: Yu Lidi was a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Yu Lidi came from Dai.

literal: In youth he trained in martial arts; his strength surpassed others, and he could shoot while galloping to either side.
idiomatic: From boyhood he trained in arms; his strength outmatched others, and he could shoot from horseback at full gallop.

literal: In the Dengguo era he was appointed Champion General and made Acting Lord of Xin'an.
idiomatic: During the Dengguo period he was made Champion General and Acting Lord of Xin'an.

literal: With Pacifier of the North General Gongsun Lan he secretly left Taiyuan, followed Han Xin's old route, opened the Jingxing Pass road, and raided Murong Bao at Zhongshan.
idiomatic: With Pacifier of the North Gongsun Lan he stole out of Taiyuan, took Han Xin's old road, opened the Jingxing route, and struck Murong Bao at Zhongshan.

literal: Daowu arrived later, saw the roads repaired, and was greatly pleased; he at once bestowed famous horses upon him.
idiomatic: Daowu came afterward, saw the roads in order, and was delighted; he immediately gave him renowned horses.

literal: When Zhao and Wei were pacified, the Emperor set out wine at a great gathering and said to Lidi, "You are my Ying and Peng!
idiomatic: After Zhao and Wei were subdued, the Emperor held a great feast and told Lidi, "You are my Ying Bu and Peng Yue!

literal: " He was advanced to Acting Duke of Xin'an.
idiomatic: He was promoted to Acting Duke of Xin'an.

literal: Daowu hunted at White Deer Mountain, saw a bear with several cubs, turned to Lidi and said, "Can you wrestle it?
idiomatic: Daowu was hunting on White Deer Mountain, saw a bear with cubs, and asked Lidi, "Can you grapple with it?

literal: " He replied, "If I wrestle and do not win, would I not have killed a stalwart in vain!
idiomatic: Lidi answered, "If I fight and fail, I would waste a brave man for nothing!

literal: I can simply drive it to the imperial presence and control it while seated.
idiomatic: Better to drive it before Your Majesty and subdue it at a distance.

literal: " Before long all were captured alive; the Emperor turned and thanked him.
idiomatic: Soon all were taken alive; the Emperor turned and thanked him.

literal: Later he became Garrison Commander of Henei.
idiomatic: He later served as Garrison Commander of Henei.

literal: When Liu Yu attacked Yao Hong, Lidi feared northern raids and built fortifications along the river.
idiomatic: When Liu Yu marched against Yao Hong, Lidi feared incursions from the north and built riverbank fortifications.

literal: Yu feared him and sent Lidi a letter asking passage westward.
idiomatic: Yu was wary of him and wrote Lidi requesting a corridor west.

literal: The letter was addressed, "Under the Black Spear Duke."
idiomatic: The superscription read, "To the Black Spear Duke's command."

literal: Lidi reported the matter; Mingyuan thereupon appointed Lidi General of the Black Spear.
idiomatic: Lidi memorialized the court; Mingyuan then made him General of the Black Spear.

literal: Lidi loved to carry a black spear; Yu saw it from afar and marveled, hence the title.
idiomatic: Lidi favored a black spear; Yu glimpsed it from afar and was struck by it, hence the name.

literal: He was transferred to Inspector of Yuzhou and advanced to Marquis of Xin'an.
idiomatic: He was moved to Inspector of Yuzhou and raised to Marquis of Xin'an.

literal: Luoyang, though a capital of successive dynasties, was in truth a frontier; Lidi labored to settle and comfort the people and won their hearts deeply.
idiomatic: Luoyang had been many dynasties' capital yet lay on the border; Lidi worked to settle the people and won them wholeheartedly.

literal: Mingyuan traveled south to Meng Ford and asked Lidi, "Can the river be bridged?
idiomatic: Mingyuan went south to Meng Ford and asked Lidi, "Can we bridge the river?

literal: " Lidi said, "Du Yu built a bridge—one may think on that precedent.
idiomatic: Lidi said, "Du Yu once bridged it; the precedent still stands.

literal: " He then lashed great boats and built a bridge at Wild Slope.
idiomatic: He moored great boats and threw a bridge across at Wild Slope.

literal: When the six armies had crossed, the Emperor sighed in deep admiration.
idiomatic: After the six armies crossed, the Emperor marveled aloud.

literal: When Taiwu campaigned against Helian Chang, he ordered Lidi and Song General Zhou Ji to strike Shancheng and drive deep into the Three Metropolises region.
idiomatic: On Taiwu's campaign against Helian Chang, Lidi and Song General Zhou Ji were sent to take Shancheng and press into the heartland.

literal: He was advanced to Duke.
idiomatic: He was promoted to duke.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Officer of the Outer Court; in judging criminal cases he won great renown.
idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to Grand Officer of the Outer Court and won fame for fair judgment.

literal: At death he was posthumously made Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Grand Commandant.

literal: Lidi from youth commanded armies until white-haired age; in affairs he judged well and wherever he went none stood before him.
idiomatic: From youth to white hair Lidi held command; he decided swiftly in the field and none could stand before him.

literal: Moreover he was humble toward scholars and did not abuse punishments; Taiwu deeply mourned him.
idiomatic: He was moreover modest toward men of worth and sparing in punishment; Taiwu grieved deeply for him.

literal: His son Luoba was handsome in bearing and skilled in repartee.
idiomatic: His son Luoba was handsome and quick in speech.

literal: He was appointed Attendant Imperial Scribe.
idiomatic: He was made Attendant Imperial Scribe.

literal: Taiwu greatly favored him and therefore bestowed the name upon him.
idiomatic: Taiwu doted on him and gave him the name Luoba.

literal: He was transferred to Supervisor of the Imperial Wardrobe Office.
idiomatic: He became Supervisor of the Imperial Wardrobe Office.

literal: Jingmu was in the Eastern Palace and treated him with great courtesy.
idiomatic: Crown Prince Jingmu in the Eastern Palace honored him warmly.

literal: Luoba always feared and avoided drawing near, not daring to court favor on his own.
idiomatic: Luoba always held back and shunned advance, not daring to court favor himself.

literal: Before long he inherited the title.
idiomatic: Soon he inherited the fief.

literal: Later he was Palace Attendant and Director of the Imperial Secretariat; the hundred officials feared him.
idiomatic: He later served as Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat; officials stood in awe of him.

literal: He died in office.
idiomatic: He died in office.

literal: Luoba had six sons.
idiomatic: Luoba had six sons.

literal: The eldest, Lie, was skilled in archery, spoke little, and had a countenance none might offend.
idiomatic: The eldest, Lie, excelled at archery, spoke little, and wore a face none dared cross.

literal: In youth he was appointed Cadet of the Feathered Forest; he was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant and Director of the Palace Secretariat.
idiomatic: Young he entered the Feathered Forest; he rose to Palace Attendant and Director of the Palace Secretariat.

literal: At that time Xiaowen was young and Empress Dowager Wenming held the regency.
idiomatic: Xiaowen was still a child and Empress Dowager Wenming ruled in his name.

literal: Lie, with Yuan Pi, Lu Rui, Li Chong, and others each received a golden tally granting that crimes would not bring death.
idiomatic: Lie, Yuan Pi, Lu Rui, Li Chong, and others each received a golden tally promising immunity from capital punishment.

literal: He was advanced to Marquis of Luoyang and transferred to Commandant of the Guard.
idiomatic: He was made Marquis of Luoyang and Commandant of the Guard.

literal: When the capital was moved to Luoyang, people's hearts clung to the old home and many objected.
idiomatic: At the transfer to Luoyang many clung to the old capital and murmured against it.

literal: The Emperor asked Lie.
idiomatic: The Emperor questioned Lie.

literal: He said, "Your Majesty's sacred design is far-reaching—not something a fool may measure.
idiomatic: Lie said, "Your Majesty's design is too deep for a fool to fathom.

literal: If I speak from the heart, those glad to move and those longing for the old are about half and half.
idiomatic: Speaking honestly, delight in the move and longing for the old divide the people evenly.

literal: " The Emperor said, "You do not lead the opposition; I deeply feel the benefit of your silence.
idiomatic: The Emperor said, "You do not stir dissent; I value deeply what you leave unsaid.

literal: He was ordered to garrison Dai while routine affairs of the rear capital were all referred to him.
idiomatic: He was sent to hold Dai; routine government at the northern capital went through him.

literal: When the imperial carriage visited Dai, he took Lie's hand and said, "The ancestral temple is weightiest; its guard is no light charge.
idiomatic: On the imperial visit to Dai the Emperor took Lie's hand and said, "The ancestral temple is paramount; guarding it is no small trust.

literal: You should reverently escort the spirit tablets and come to Luoyang in due time.
idiomatic: Escort the spirit tablets with reverence and join us at Luoyang in good time.

literal: Lie with Prince of Gaoyang Yong escorted the spirit lords to Luoyang and was transferred to Minister of the Household.
idiomatic: Lie and Prince Yong of Gaoyang brought the spirit lords to Luoyang; he was then made Minister of the Household.

literal: In the nineteenth year, in the great selection of officials, Lie's son Deng cited precedent and sought advancement.
idiomatic: In year nineteen, during the great selection, Lie's son Deng invoked precedent to seek promotion.

literal: Lie memorialized that he himself had never taught his son and asked that Deng be dismissed.
idiomatic: Lie submitted that he had never trained his son and begged Deng's removal.

literal: The Emperor said, "These are words of discernment—I did not think Lie could see so clearly!
idiomatic: The Emperor said, "That is the speech of a man who knows his mind—I did not expect such clarity from Lie!

literal: " He then summoned Deng and decreed, "I now establish rites in the new capital and raise men throughout the realm; your father has shown a modest memorial and the bearing of an upright man—therefore I advance you to Assistant Commander of the Crown Prince's Guard.
idiomatic: He summoned Deng and said, "I am founding rites in the new capital and seeking talent across the land; your father's modest petition and upright manner move me—I advance you to Assistant Commander of the Crown Prince's Guard.

literal: " Lie was further made Regular Attendant and enfeoffed as Viscount of Liaocheng.
idiomatic: Lie was also made Regular Attendant and enfeoffed Viscount of Liaocheng.

literal: When Mu Tai and Lu Rui plotted rebellion at the old capital, the Emperor went to Dai and Tai and the rest were executed.
idiomatic: When Mu Tai and Lu Rui conspired at the old capital, the Emperor went to Dai; Tai and his fellows were put to death.

literal: Lie and Li Chong were granted imperial letters setting forth the intent of the golden tally.
idiomatic: Lie and Li Chong received sealed letters reaffirming the golden tally's promise.

literal: At that time many of the old clans of Dai shared the guilt, yet Lie's house alone was untouched.
idiomatic: Many Dai clans of the day were implicated, but Lie's lineage alone stayed clean.

literal: The Emperor valued him all the more.
idiomatic: The Emperor prized him still more.

literal: He sighed and said, "Yuan Yan is decisive in authority and favor and holds himself in no low regard, yet in whole-hearted loyalty and fierce resolve he is not Lie's equal.
idiomatic: He sighed, "Yuan Yan is sharp in reward and punishment and thinks well of himself, yet in loyal daring he falls short of Lie.

literal: Had Lie been at Dai then, he would at once have beheaded the ringleaders of the Five Three clans.
idiomatic: Had Lie been in Dai that day, he would have struck off the Five Three chiefs at once.

literal: Lie in integrity does not yield to Jin Midi.
idiomatic: Lie in moral fiber does not bow to Jin Midi.

literal: " He was ordered made General of the Guards.
idiomatic: He was appointed General of the Guards.

literal: In that office he followed the campaign in Jing and Mian and was given an additional suite of martial music.
idiomatic: He marched on Jing and Mian in that rank and received an extra band of martial music.

literal: In the twenty-third year, Qi general Chen Xianda invaded Maquan; the Emperor, ill in his carriage, went to attack him.
idiomatic: In year twenty-three Chen Xianda of Qi invaded Maquan; the Emperor, sick in camp, went out against him.

literal: He took Lie's hand and entrusted the capital to him.
idiomatic: He clasped Lie's hand and entrusted the capital to his care.

literal: The Emperor died at the traveling palace; Prince of Pengcheng Xie concealed the death and returned.
idiomatic: The Emperor died on campaign; Prince Xie of Pengcheng hid the tidings and turned homeward.

literal: In the Emperor's name he summoned Xuanwu to meet the carriage at Luyang.
idiomatic: He issued orders in the late Emperor's name summoning Xuanwu to join the train at Luyang.

literal: Because Lie's charge as defender was weighty, he secretly reported the calamitous news.
idiomatic: Knowing Lie's weight as defender, he secretly sent word of the death.

literal: Lie disposed the rear guard without change in spirit or bearing.
idiomatic: Lie arranged the rear guard; his composure never wavered.

literal: When Xuanwu took the throne, favor toward him was as before.
idiomatic: When Xuanwu succeeded, Lie's favor stood as before.

literal: Prince of Xianyang Xi was chief minister and his power matched the age.
idiomatic: Prince Xi of Xianyang was chief minister and his power dominated the court.

literal: He once sent a household slave to speak to Lie, asking for former Feathered Forest guards to bear arms on his comings and goings.
idiomatic: Xi once sent a house slave to Lie requesting old Feathered Forest guards to carry arms in his train.

literal: Lie refused.
idiomatic: Lie refused.

literal: Xi sent word to Lie, "I am the Son of Heaven's son and the Son of Heaven's uncle; a chief minister's command—how does it differ from an edict?
idiomatic: Xi sent word: "I am the emperor's son and uncle; a chief minister's order—how is it not an edict?

literal: " Lie answered sternly, "I never said Your Highness was not the Son of Heaven's son and uncle.
idiomatic: Lie answered coldly, "I never denied you were the emperor's son and uncle.

literal: If this were an edict, it should be sent through the proper officials.
idiomatic: Had it been an edict, proper officers would have borne it.

literal: If you send a private slave to demand the state's Feathered Forest, you may have my head, but you will not have the guards!
idiomatic: Send a private slave to seize the imperial guard, and you may have my head—but not my guards!

literal: " Xi hated Lie's rigidity and had him sent out as Inspector of Hengzhou.
idiomatic: Xi hated Lie's stiffness and posted him Inspector of Hengzhou.

literal: Lie did not wish a frontier appointment and said to Prince Xie of Pengcheng, "Has Your Highness forgotten the late Emperor's charge at Nanyang?
idiomatic: Lie, unwilling to take a province, told Prince Xie of Pengcheng, "Have you forgotten the late Emperor's charge at Nanyang?

literal: Yet you drive an old man even to this!
idiomatic: And you press an old man so far!

literal: " He thereupon pleaded illness and resigned.
idiomatic: He pleaded illness and withdrew.

literal: Xuanwu, because Xi and others monopolized power, secretly plotted to remove them.
idiomatic: Xuanwu, seeing Xi and his faction monopolize power, secretly planned their removal.

literal: In the first month of the second year of Jingming, at the spring offering, the Three Dukes fasted at the temple.
idiomatic: In the first month of Jingming year two, at the spring rites, the Three Dukes kept fast at the temple.

literal: At night the Emperor summoned Lie's son Zhong and said, "Your father should come early tomorrow.
idiomatic: That night the Emperor called Lie's son Zhong and said, "Let your father come early tomorrow.

literal: " At dawn Lie arrived.
idiomatic: At dawn Lie came.

literal: The decree said, "The imperial uncles are arrogant and slack; I wish you to summon them with troops—will you go?
idiomatic: The edict ran, "My uncles grow insolent; I would have you summon them under arms—will you go?

literal: " Lie said, "This old servant has served successive reigns and is known somewhat for resolve and courage.
idiomatic: Lie said, "I have served many reigns and am known, if at all, for boldness.

literal: Today's affair is one I dare not refuse.
idiomatic: Today's task I dare not refuse.

literal: " He then led more than sixty men including the Direct Attendants, proclaimed the intent, and summoned Prince Xi of Xianyang, Prince Xie of Pengcheng, and Prince Xiang of Beihai, escorting them to the Emperor.
idiomatic: He took sixty-odd Direct Attendants and heralds, summoned Princes Xi of Xianyang, Xie of Pengcheng, and Xiang of Beihai, and brought them before the throne.

literal: Each prince bowed his head and returned his authority.
idiomatic: Each bowed low and surrendered his powers.
